faq.a: By length: values with 12 or more digits are treated as milliseconds, shorter ones as seconds — and the detected unit is always shown so you can sanity-check it.
faq.q: How does it know if my timestamp is seconds or milliseconds?

faq.a: Both. Results show your browser's local time and UTC side by side, so you never have to guess which one a log used.

whenNotToUse: Timestamps carry no time zone of their own — a value that looks wrong by a few hours is usually a zone mix-up in the system that produced it, not a conversion error.
Dates far outside the range your browser can represent (before 271,822 BC or after 275,760 AD) can't be converted.
